attestations.notes: Read current proof: nonempty first-order domain supplies a; Separation with z≠z gives an empty set; Extensionality proves uniqueness. The empty case is the conclusion, not an assumed set.
Read current proof: x≠∅ gives B∈x; Separation on B gives the universal-membership class; B∈x makes the B restriction redundant, and Extensionality removes choice of B.
Read current proof: Power Set provides an ambient set of all subsets, Separation removes surplus members, and Extensionality proves uniqueness; x=∅ remains covered.
Read five cases: union over ∅ is empty, singleton and pair union reduce to membership disjunction; nonempty singleton/pair intersections reduce to conjunction; Extensionality closes each.
Read current proof: a,b∈A∪B imply {a},{a,b}⊆A∪B; Kuratowski pair is a subset of P(A∪B), hence belongs to P(P(A∪B)).
Read both directions and equal/unequal cases: equality forces each endpoint into the other pair; when a=b both c,d=a, otherwise the two possible matchings exhaust; singleton specialization follows.
Read both directions for Kuratowski pairs: unordered-pair equality yields the direct or crossed singleton case; each forces a=c and b=d, including coincident components.
Read current proof: each component of a Kuratowski pair in R lies in ∪∪R; Separation on that ambient set forms both domain and range, including R=∅.

Read current proof: Infinity supplies I0; first-order Separation defines intersection of all inductive sets inside I0; zero and successor closure prove inductiveness, and mutual inclusion proves uniqueness.
Read current proof: a zero-containing successor-closed subset of omega is inductive, hence contains minimal omega; property form follows by Separation and conversely by membership property.
Read induction on von Neumann naturals: empty base; successor transitivity follows from n transitive; either alleged self-membership case yields n∈n, contradicting the hypothesis.

Read current minimal-closed-relation proof: intersect closed subsets of N×A, use induction for totality, P1 to fix the zero value, P1/P2 plus uniqueness at n to force uniqueness at sigma(n), then induction for uniqueness of functions. Ambient powerset/separation constructions are standard ZFC.
Read current proof: induction gives P3; sigma(n) contains n so cannot be zero; if sigma(m)=sigma(n) and m≠n, transitivity yields n∈n, proving P2.
Read current proof: apply recursion on omega with initial m and successor function; uniqueness gives each s_m, and the defining equations give total binary addition.
Read induction on c: zero uses right identity; successor rewrites both sides by the recursion equation and the induction hypothesis.
Read induction on n: zero is definitional and successor follows by applying sigma to the hypothesis; right identity is the defining zero clause.
Read induction on n: zero is definitional; successor uses recursion twice and the induction hypothesis to commute sigma with left addition.
Read induction on n: zero uses established left identity; successor uses recursion and the separately proved left-successor law.
Read induction on the common right summand k: zero is immediate; successor equality reduces by injectivity of sigma to the inductive hypothesis.
Read induction on the set of zero-or-successor naturals: zero is in it and every successor has a predecessor witness, so it is all of omega.

Read current proof: positive addends cannot leave a number unchanged by cancellation; incompatible strict directions force a nonzero sum to be zero; induction on n gives comparability, splitting a positive witness as a successor.
Read current proof: reflexivity and transitivity use addition; trichotomy gives totality; cancellation and the fact a zero sum has zero summands give antisymmetry.

Read both directions: a strict order witness is a nonzero successor, converting m+j=n to sigma(m)+i=n; conversely sigma(m)+i=n becomes m+sigma(i)=n and cancellation excludes equality. Immediate-successor conclusion follows.

Read current proof: each pair in R has coordinates in dom R and ran R; the iff for R⊆A×B follows by ordered-pair injectivity in the forward direction and coordinate membership in reverse, including R=∅.
Read current proof: inverse and composite pairs lie in the displayed domain/range products, so Separation forms them; restriction is Separation inside R. Empty relations cause no exception.
Read induction: P1 gives zero base; P2 turns a successor fixed point into the forbidden predecessor fixed point.

Read entire current proof: induction makes omega transitive, establishes membership implies additive order and then the converse using m<sigma(n) iff m≤n; trichotomy plus n∉n gives m≤n iff m⊆n. Zero and successor cases are explicit; no ordinal result is used.

Read full five-claim proof: a codomain transposition sends the top domain point sigma(n) to n; restricting the remaining injection gives forbidden sigma(n)→n. Order-as-membership handles smaller codomains and N; a transposition removing a missing point proves finite Dedekind finiteness; trichotomy proves equal finite cardinalities. Checked n=0 and no-choice use.

Read contradiction proof: the set T of n with no S element ≤n contains zero if S has no least, and successor closure uses discreteness to exclude all earlier S points; induction forces S empty, contradiction.
Read recursion application with initial zero and add_m endomap; uniqueness of p_m and the recursive equations give a total multiplication.
Read both directions of ≤ using associativity, commutativity and right cancellation; equality cancellation converts the strict order in both directions.
Read unit proof: right unit follows at sigma(0), while joint induction establishes zero times n and one times n, including n=0.
Read both inductions: the n induction establishes sigma(a)·n=a·n+n using only addition laws; the c induction establishes a·(b+c)=a·b+a·c. Zero and successor equations align.
Read induction on n: zero uses 0·m=0; successor uses recursive right multiplication and the independently established left successor law.
Read induction on c: zero uses multiplication zero clause; successor uses recursion and left distributivity to align the two products.
Read contrapositive: nonzero factors are successors, so m·n=m·b+sigma(a)=sigma(m·b+a), nonzero by Peano P1.
Read current proof: distributivity preserves a nonnegative difference d; if d and k are nonzero, no-zero-divisors and additive cancellation make the product difference strict.
Read quotient-pair proof: the two representative equations add and regroup to the equivalence of sums; commuting one equality gives equivalence of swapped pairs for negation.
Read current proof: the cross-term expansions agree when the first pair changes; symmetry of the product formula applies the same reasoning to the second pair.

Read representative calculations: quotient well-definedness licenses them; additive group laws and multiplication identity, associativity, commutativity, distributivity follow by the displayed natural-number expansions.

Read proof of representative independence via adding equal cross terms and natural order cancellation; checked transitivity, addition compatibility, and positive product expansion with nonzero natural gaps k,m.
Read field-axiom proof: distributivity makes 0·a idempotent under addition; additive cancellation against 0·a yields 0·a=0.
Read cone proof: translation preserves b−a, and summing two strict inequalities adds two positive differences, which stays in the cone.
Read distributivity proof of (-a)b=−ab and a(-b)=−ab; uniqueness of additive inverses then gives (-a)(-b)=ab.

Read five claims: cone multiplication proves positive products; field negation identities prove mixed and double negative signs; both directions of positive and negative order multiplication use trichotomy to exclude equality and reverse ordering.
Read two trichotomy cases for a≠0: a or −a lies in the positive cone; closure and (-a)^2=a^2 prove the conclusion.
Read proof: field axiom 1≠0 and positivity of every nonzero square give 1=1²>0.
Read proof: a positive element has nonzero inverse; a negative inverse would make 1 negative, contradicting 1>0. Multiplication by positive a⁻¹b⁻¹ reverses reciprocal magnitudes for 0<a<b.
Read four sign patterns using integer ordered-ring positivity and ring negation; nonzero product follows, and applying it to (x−y)z proves cancellation.
Read group-axiom calculations: two identities coincide and two inverses coincide in both additive group and nonzero multiplicative group; uniqueness is appropriately restricted to x≠0 for inverses.
Read cross-multiplication checks for product, sum, and negation of integer fractions; nonzero denominators remain nonzero by the integer domain result.
Read representative calculations for ring axioms, distributivity, 1≠0 and inverse (b,a) when a≠0; integer no-zero-divisors keeps denominators nonzero.

Read current proof and def-rat-order: every rational has a positive-denominator representative. Positive scaling in ordered integers proves representative independence, transitivity and additive compatibility; positive numerators and denominators give positive products.
Read current proof: evaluating e*f once via left identity and once via right identity gives equality without associativity; both uniqueness corollaries apply the same two-sided comparison.
Read current monoid proof: h=h*(g*h′)=(h*g)*h′=h′ by associativity and identity; this yields existence from both one-sided inverses and uniqueness for an already invertible element.
Read recursive ordered-field proof: 1>0 and adding 1 preserves positivity and gives strict increase; inductions on n establish additivity and multiplicativity of the canonical natural embedding.

Read pair-model proof: equality of (m,0),(n,0) forces m=n; operation formulas preserve addition and multiplication; integer order reduces to natural order; a≥b represents the unique nonnegative difference.
